sprint: Magic Publish — the World beat now stages per object. Reported in one line: "magic publish should stage world owned objects." Artwork and Decorations already arrived one at a time, so a two-picture Scene read as two moments; the World's own Layer Pack furniture — the wall, the caption, the wax seal — still arrived as a single backdrop beat, which reads as a slide template snapping into place rather than as a place being assembled. The whole reveal is a choreographed decomposition of the FINISHED page by layer (no history, no timeline, no snapshots, nothing hooked into autosave), so staging the World needed only to name which layer arrived when.
task:
THE ONE REAL DESIGN DECISION: World partial staging is INDEX-based, not id-based. The scope-filtered layer pack lives behind renderer/slideRenderer.js's own _activeLayerPack, and duplicating a keying scheme across the two files would risk exactly the drift their own comments warn about — so js/magicReveal.js's new _worldArrivals enumerates the SAME scope-filtered array and a partial stage carries indices into it. That contract only holds if both files resolve the same pack, which was traced end to end rather than assumed: _worldLayers tries ThemeEngine.getActiveArtworkTheme() then getActiveTheme(); _activeLayerPack uses _layoutTheme(s) = s.layoutTheme -> _artworkTheme(s) -> getActiveTheme(), and _artworkTheme returns s.artworkTheme directly when set, which buildPayload sets from getActiveArtworkTheme() while carrying metadata verbatim — so the same pack and the same layoutId, in the same order. Layer pack array order IS paint order, so a full-bleed backdrop naturally arrives first.

js/magicReveal.js: _worldLayers / _worldArrivals / _hasWorldFurniture added; the world beat joins the arrivals dispatch beside artwork and decorations, so _arrivalSteps splits it into up to MAX_ARRIVALS_PER_GROUP steps exactly like the others; _stageSlide's setFor tri-state now drives the World too — an empty Set sets _magicHideLayerPack (hide all), null leaves both markers off (show all), a populated Set writes _magicLayerPackShown indices. Markers rather than a filtered theme because the resolved theme is shared ThemeEngine state a Magic stage must never reach into. The module still never mutates the slide it is handed.

renderer/slideRenderer.js: _activeLayerPack honours the new _magicLayerPackShown alongside the existing _magicHideLayerPack, filtering the scope-filtered array by index; buildPayload carries it. Absent both markers — every ordinary payload — they resolve false/null and every existing render is byte-identical.

js/storyDestinations.js: a full-bleed backdrop is deliberately EXEMPT from the arrival motion. Its rect IS the page, so 'arrival' would scale and lift the entire frame — the camera moving, not an object landing — and the roadmap's own animation table already says a background washes in. New _magicRectIsFullBleed measures against the page's own MAPPED extents rather than the canvas, because a 4:5 page inside a 9:16 frame is letterboxed and comparing to the canvas would answer "no" for exactly the case being looked for; such a frame gets 'wash' and carries no arrivalRect, so nobody later mistakes a rect for something that mattered.

Verified 35/35, zero page errors, via a new magic_world_stage_verify suite whose fixture World carries a full-bleed wash, a badge, a seal and one deliberately invisible layer: A — enumeration order, indices, the invisible layer skipped, an ordinary payload carrying both markers resolving to no-staging; B — three visible layers give three World frames naming each layer in paint order, blank still leads, World precedes Artwork, and a World that places nothing gets no beat at all; C — the index lists grow [0], [0,1], [0,1,2], the caller's own slide is untouched and every stage is its own object; D — PIXEL PROOF that the renderer honours the list, sampling three points deliberately clear of the Place across all five frames; E — the backdrop washes with no rect while the badge and seal arrive with rects, and no wash frame carries a stray one; F — zero page errors.

ONE TEST-SIDE FIX, disclosed and not an app bug: B5 originally made its bare-World page by setting slide.layoutTheme, but that is a PAYLOAD-only field the Screen 2 carousel sets (creationFlow.js) and nothing reads off a slide, so the premise was inert — rewritten to stub the two ThemeEngine accessors _worldLayers actually calls, which works because the top-level const and window.ThemeEngine are one shared object.
